title: Revenue tile leaves out a reversed or voided invoice, like the Sales report
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
  2. In the top bar, click the location name at the top left (e.g. ShopHub) and choose your test location: one where nobody else invoices, issues credits or clocks time this week. The next step checks that it is quiet. If no location you can reach is quiet, create one once and reuse it on every later run: Settings > Locations > add a location (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dashboard Quiet") > save, give your user access, then choose it here. Locations cannot be deleted, so never create a second one.
  3. Check the location is quiet: click Dashboard in the top menu, click the range pill on the Revenue tile and choose This Week. Revenue must read $0.00 with 0 Invoices under it. If it shows anything else, choose another location.
  4. Run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  5. Create a test customer: Customers > New Customer, name it (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1") and save. On its Contacts tab add a contact (e.g. "Dana Test"). On its Assets tab add an asset (e.g. unit "ZZ-101") and pick that contact in the asset's Contact field.
  6. Create and invoice three work orders (A, B and C) for this customer, each with these standard steps:
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer and its asset > Create.
    • In the work order header set Service Advisor to "Alex Advisor" and enter the mileage (e.g. 123456). If the Finance tab is greyed out with "Please select a contact for the asset", choose the contact and answer YES to keep it on the asset.
    • Lines tab > New Line: Description "ZZAUTOTEST Line", Technician "Tom Tech", Labor Rate e.g. $100.00 per hour, Estimated Time 3.00 for A, 5.00 for B, 2.00 for C, Tech Time the same hours, tick Approved > Save & Close.
    • On each line type a Story (e.g. "Done") and set the line to Complete. Then click Complete Work Order, then Mark Reviewed.
    • Finance tab > Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment dialog opens, close it without taking a payment. Do not send or pay the invoice.
    • On the Finance tab write down the invoice's Subtotal (before any discount and before tax), e.g. A $300.00, B $500.00, C $200.00. If shop supplies are added automatically they are part of the subtotal: use the subtotal the invoice shows.
  7. Leave invoice C unpaid and unsent: it is the one you will void. (A line added to a sent or paid invoice splits the work order instead of voiding.)
  8. Your role must be able to reverse an invoice (Admin can): the Reverse item sits in the invoice's three dots on the Finance tab.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu, set the Revenue tile's range pill to This Week and write down the figure (expected $1,000.00 = $300.00 + $500.00 + $200.00).
  2. Click Work Orders, open work order B, click the Finance tab, click the invoice's three dots > Reverse, and confirm Reverse.
  3. Click Dashboard, set Revenue to This Week again and write down the figure.
  4. Click Work Orders and open work order C.
  5. On the Lines tab click New Line: Description "ZZAUTOTEST Extra", Labor Rate e.g. $100.00 per hour, Estimated Time 0.50, Tech Time 0.50, tick Approved > Save & Close. (This voids C's unpaid invoice.)
  6. Type a Story on the new line, set it to Complete, then click Complete Work Order and Mark Reviewed.
  7. Click the Finance tab and write down what it shows for C's first invoice (for example a Void label).
  8. Click Create Invoice, close the New Customer Payment dialog without paying, and write down the new Subtotal (e.g. $250.00 = $200.00 + 0.50 hour x $100.00).
  9. Click Dashboard, set Revenue to This Week and write down the figure.
  10. Click the arrow icon beside "Revenue" on the tile (its tooltip names the report).
  11. On the Sales report set the Date control to This week and write down every invoice row and the Totals row Subtotal.
  12. Try to make an invoice with no customer: Parts > Part Sales > New Part Sale, and see whether it can be invoiced without choosing a customer. If the screen insists on a customer, stop this step.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: Revenue reads $1,000.00 ($300.00 + $500.00 + $200.00).
  • After reversing B: Revenue reads $500.00 ($300.00 + $200.00). The reversed invoice adds nothing.
  • After voiding C's first invoice and re-invoicing: Revenue reads $550.00 ($300.00 + $250.00). The voided $200.00 invoice adds nothing and the new $250.00 invoice counts.
  • The Sales report for This week lists A and C's new invoice only (no row for B and none for C's voided invoice), and its Totals row Subtotal reads $550.00, the same as the tile.
  • If you could invoice a sale with no customer, its subtotal is in both the Revenue figure and the Sales report total. If you could not, write "no-customer invoice not reachable by hand" in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-E2 and its context note, S3-R1). Tech plan section 7 (2026-09-16) informs how a void is produced by hand: Reverse removes the invoice, and a line added to a still-unpaid invoiced work order voids it.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-E2: “A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.”
  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S3-E2 context note (Sales report): “That is a defect in the Sales report rather than a dashboard decision, and it is corrected inside this project so Revenue can match it (@chris ruling, 2026-09-15). Correcting it moves the Sales report's own existing totals for any range containing voided or no-company invoices, so it ships with a release note.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
